## 1. The wrapped one  (`#the-wrapped-one`)

Cited ayat: 73:1-8

> **73:1** بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمُزَّمِّلُ
>
> **73:2** قُمِ ٱلَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
>
> **73:3** نِّصْفَهُۥٓ أَوِ ٱنقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا
>
> **73:4** أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَرْتِيلًا
>
> **73:5** إِنَّا سَنُلْقِى عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا
>
> **73:6** إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ ٱلَّيْلِ هِىَ أَشَدُّ وَطْـًٔا وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلًا
>
> **73:7** إِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ سَبْحًا طَوِيلًا
>
> **73:8** وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًا

### Claims

**c1** (73:1): The passage opens with a call to the one addressed by the word al-muzzammil, often rendered the wrapped one.

**c2** (73:2-4): The one addressed is told to stand through the night except for a little: half of it, or a little less than that, or more than that; and to recite the Quran in measured fashion.

**c3** (73:5): God says that He will cast upon the one addressed a weighty word.

**c4** (73:6): The rising of the night is firmer in tread and more upright in speech.

**c5** (73:7): By day the one addressed has long occupation.

**c6** (73:8): The one addressed is told to remember the name of his Lord and to devote himself to Him with complete devotion.

### One-minute summary

The passage calls on the one addressed as the wrapped one [c1]. He is told to stand through the night except for a little, and to recite the Quran in measured fashion [c2]. God says that He will cast upon him a weighty word [c3], and he is told to remember the name of his Lord and devote himself to Him [c6].

### Complete story

The passage opens with a call to the one addressed by the word al-muzzammil, often rendered the wrapped one [c1].

He is told to stand through the night except for a little: half of it, or a little less than that, or more than that; and to recite the Quran in measured fashion [c2]. God says that He will cast upon him a weighty word [c3].

The passage says that the rising of the night is firmer in tread and more upright in speech [c4], and that by day he has long occupation [c5]. He is told to remember the name of his Lord and to devote himself to Him with complete devotion [c6].

### Deep study

The call and the commands are addressed to one person, whom the verses do not name [c1]. The commands are about the night [c2], and the passage gives reasons from the night and the day [c4][c5]. The weighty word that God will cast upon him is not described [c3]. The passage ends with remembrance and devotion [c6].

### Kids mode

The passage calls to someone who is wrapped up, and tells him to stand through the night except for a little [c1][c2]. He is told to recite the Quran slowly and clearly [c2]. He is told to remember the name of his Lord [c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage joins the quiet of the night to speech that is more upright [c4]. Another is that it places remembrance of the Lord's name beside the long occupation of the day [c5][c6].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who is addressed. The call is by a title and the verses name no one.
- Not established: why the one addressed is called the wrapped one, or what he was wrapped in; the verses give no circumstance.
- Not established: what the weighty word is, or when it was cast.
- Not established: for whom the standing through the night was meant beyond the one addressed, or for how long. The later verses of the same surah are outside this draft.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identity of the one addressed and the occasion of the call. Neither is used in the story texts.

## 2. The cloaked one  (`#the-cloaked-one`)

Cited ayat: 74:1-7

> **74:1** بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمُدَّثِّرُ
>
> **74:2** قُمْ فَأَنذِرْ
>
> **74:3** وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ
>
> **74:4** وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ
>
> **74:5** وَٱلرُّجْزَ فَٱهْجُرْ
>
> **74:6** وَلَا تَمْنُن تَسْتَكْثِرُ
>
> **74:7** وَلِرَبِّكَ فَٱصْبِرْ

### Claims

**c1** (74:1): The passage opens with a call to the one addressed by the word al-muddaththir, often rendered the cloaked one.

**c2** (74:2): The one addressed is told to arise and warn.

**c3** (74:3): He is told to magnify his Lord.

**c4** (74:4): He is told to purify his garments; the Arabic word is read in more than one way.

**c5** (74:5): He is told to keep away from ar-rujz, a word whose sense is disputed.

**c6** (74:6): He is told not to give in order to gain more; the phrase is read in more than one way.

**c7** (74:7): He is told to be patient for the sake of his Lord.

### One-minute summary

The passage calls on the one addressed as the cloaked one [c1]. He is told to arise and warn [c2], to magnify his Lord [c3], and to be patient for the sake of his Lord [c7].

### Complete story

The passage opens with a call to the one addressed by the word al-muddaththir, often rendered the cloaked one [c1].

He is told to arise and warn [c2], and to magnify his Lord [c3]. He is told to purify his garments; the Arabic word is read in more than one way [c4]. He is told to keep away from ar-rujz, a word whose sense is disputed [c5], and not to give in order to gain more, a phrase that is also read in more than one way [c6].

The passage ends by telling him to be patient for the sake of his Lord [c7].

### Deep study

A series of short commands follow one another, and the passage gives no reason for any of them [c2][c3][c4][c5][c6][c7]. Some of them are read in more than one way: the word for garments, the word ar-rujz, and the phrase about giving in order to gain more [c4][c5][c6]. The warning has no stated object [c2].

### Kids mode

The passage calls to someone covered up, and tells him to arise and warn [c1][c2]. He is told to magnify his Lord [c3]. He is told to be patient for the sake of his Lord [c7].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage places patience for the sake of the Lord at the end of a series of commands [c7]. Another is that the commands to warn and to magnify the Lord stand side by side [c2][c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who is addressed, or why he is called the cloaked one. The call is by a title and the verses name no one.
- Not established: whom or what he was to warn; the verse has no object.
- Not established: what ar-rujz refers to, whether the garments in 74:4 are clothing or something else, or what the phrase about giving in order to gain more refers to.
- Not established: whether this passage came before or after the previous chapter's; the chapters follow the inventory order.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identity of the one addressed and the occasion of the call. Neither is used in the story texts.
